Create a Complete UNO Deck

create_uno_deck.Rd

Constructs a full UNO card deck consisting of 108 cards, following official game rules. This includes number cards (0–9), action cards (Skip, Reverse, +2), and wild cards (Wild, Wild Draw 4). The resulting deck is returned as a tidy tibble and is sorted by color, type, and value.

Usage

create_uno_deck()

Value

A tibble with exactly 108 rows and 3 columns:

  • color – Card color: one of "red", "green", "blue", "yellow", or "wild"

  • value – Card value: a string representing number, action, or wild type (e.g., "5", "+2", "wild_draw4")

  • type – Card type: one of "number", "action", or "wild"

Details

Each of the four colors (red, green, blue, yellow) includes:

  • One 0 card

  • Two of each number card from 1–9

  • Two of each action card: "skip", "reverse", "+2"

Additionally:

  • Four "wild" cards

  • Four "wild_draw4" cards

- This function uses expand_grid() and uncount() to generate and replicate UNO cards.
- Number and action cards are repeated according to official UNO rules.
- The function returns a tibble with 108 cards structured for use in simulations.

This deck can be passed directly to downstream functions such as deal_hands or play_game.

Examples

# Generate the UNO deck
deck <- create_uno_deck()

# Validate the total card count
nrow(deck)  # Should return 108
#> [1] 108

# Check card distribution
table(deck$type)
#> 
#> action number   wild 
#>     24     76      8 

# Preview color types
unique(deck$color)
#> [1] "blue"   "green"  "red"    "wild"   "yellow"

# Use the deck to deal to players
hands <- deal_hands(deck, n_players = 4)
sapply(hands$hands, nrow)
#> Player_1 Player_2 Player_3 Player_4 
#>        7        7        7        7
